key_insight: The paper shows that finite Euler ensembles split into parity-defined sectors, where odd and punctured-even cases become marginal Lyapunov limits while even zero-winding modes remain genuinely unstable.
engineering_relevance: This gives a mathematically controlled way to identify which reduced turbulence states are stable, marginal, or singular, helping guide reduced-order models and spectral diagnostics for decaying incompressible flows.
method: Solve the tangential linearized problem exactly at finite cutoff using the Ising history only through the closure winding.
Decompose the continuum limit into odd, even zero-winding, and punctured-even sectors using parity and rational-angle arithmetic.
Analyze the surviving spectral edge with coprime cotangent sums, Jordan totients, Dirichlet convolution, and zeta-function asymptotics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact solvability at finite N and asymptotic partition-function and eigenvalue results, including Z_e,0(N)/Z_e,*(N) ~ 6N/pi^2 and weak convergence of normalized eigenvalues to delta_0 in the marginal sectors.
watch_item: The zero-winding even sector is a singular discrete zero mode rather than part of the Gaussian continuum, so implementations must separate it explicitly to avoid mixing unstable and marginal spectra.
paper_title: The Euler Ensemble as a Turbulent Attractor: Parity Sectors, Zero Modes, and a Zeta Edge
